fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Vehicle Parking Area; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Dense Vegetation
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space; Multiple Structures
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the access drive entrance clearly so responders can distinguish it from neighboring driveways or road shoulders at night.
• Clear vegetation along both sides of the access drive so responders can move through without obstruction.
• Trim any dense vegetation that overhangs or narrows the access drive to maintain full vehicle width clearance.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of stored items so arriving apparatus have room to stage.
• Identify and mark a designated turnaround point near the structures so responders are not forced to back out the full length of the access drive.
• Post a visible property map or address placard near the driveway entrance showing the locations of both structures.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between buildings on foot without navigating through dense vegetation.
• Cut back dense vegetation adjacent to both structures to allow responders to move around the exterior walls.
• Maintain the open lawn area free of parked vehicles and stored equipment so it can be used as a staging area if needed.
• Confirm the access drive surface can support the weight of a fire engine or ambulance, and repair any soft or eroded sections that could trap a vehicle.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Large Trees; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Trees; Open Terrain; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Vegetation Along Driveway; Scattered Shrubs; Ground Vegetation; Single Access Route; Limited Rear Access
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree cluster closest to the structure to create open space between individual trees and the building.
• Trim branches on large trees that extend directly over or toward the roof and walls of the structure.
• Remove shrubs and low-growing plants that are growing directly against the sides of the structure.
• Clear ground vegetation within the immediate area surrounding the structure.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure so there is visible open space between their canopies and the building.
• Trim overhanging branches along the driveway so vehicles, including large emergency vehicles, can pass through without obstruction.
• Remove shrubs and ground vegetation growing along the edges of the driveway that could spread fire toward the travel path.
• Keep the single access route clear of fallen branches, overgrown vegetation, and other obstructions at all times.
• Cut back vegetation on the rear of the property to open up movement and visibility around the back of the structure.
• Remove dead material from scattered shrubs near the structure.
• Keep ground vegetation mowed or cut short in open areas immediately surrounding the structure.
• Separate shrub groupings near the structure so there are visible gaps rather than continuous plant cover between them and the building.
